benchmark.category: a story-driven, cartoon-styled educational space mission design game for middle schoolers
benchmark.users: middle-school children (gimnaziu) playing a three-level NASA-themed mission story with a sarcastic robot, and the Space Apps judges who review the finished game

requirements.source_phrase: First, there is the storyline (the BOB robot makes an introduction), then there are the attached dialogues and scenes between the characters (also as attachment).
requirements.statement: Opening the app shows a title screen in English with a visible start control; pressing it plays B.O.B.'s introduction dialogue and then moves the player into the first level.
requirements.notes: Entry point of the whole game; the app has no auth, so the title screen is the only entry surface.

requirements.statement: GET / serves the built single-page app shell and its JS bundle with HTTP 200 for the root and for any deep path, and the bundle executes with no missing-module or undefined-name error so every stage of the game is reachable.
requirements.notes: Build description: /app/frontend/src/App.js stage machine; every screen requirement depends on this shell being served.

requirements.source_phrase: neapărat jocul să fie în limba engleză, nu română
requirements.statement: Every screen, button, dialogue line, quiz question, malfunction label, ending, colony message and credit appears in English, with no Romanian sentence anywhere in the running game.
requirements.notes: The brief is bilingual; the user explicitly reverses the Romanian framing and requires English-only copy.

requirements.statement: The shipped bundle and every data module it imports contain only English user-facing strings: a scan of the served JS for the brief's Romanian words ('racheta', 'greșeli', 'Reia quiz-ul', 'încarc') returns no user-facing occurrence.
requirements.notes: Checks the language rule at the data level, where the quiz/dialogue text actually lives.

requirements.source_phrase: then there are the attached dialogues and scenes between the characters (also as attachment)
requirements.statement: On the intro and between levels the dialogue plays as a sequence of scenes between the named characters, each scene showing its speaker, its English line and the character art, and a click advances to the next line without the sequence stalling.
requirements.notes: Dialogue content comes from an attachment not available in the conversation; only structure and language are assertable.

requirements.statement: The dialogue script served with the build defines, for every scene, an ordered list of speaker/line pairs in English, and the stage machine reads it with no undefined access.
requirements.notes: Mechanism the dialogue screen depends on.

requirements.source_phrase: the images for the characters that are already created (attachments)
requirements.statement: Every character who speaks in the dialogue shows the portrait supplied in the attachments at its declared size, un-stretched and fully inside its frame, rather than a broken-image icon or a substitute image.
requirements.notes: User supplied character art and expects it used.

requirements.statement: Every character image, colony photograph and sound file the build references is served by the app's own host with HTTP 200, an image or audio content type and a non-zero body at the URL the bundle requests.
requirements.notes: Mechanism every art and audio requirement depends on.

requirements.source_phrase: robotul B.O.B. este sarcastic, face glume (încarc fișierul cu scenarii posibile, glume care să fie puse pe parcursul aplicației)
requirements.statement: B.O.B.'s lines carry sarcastic jokes drawn from the supplied jokes file at more than one point in the game, with at least one joke line visible on the introduction, on a between-level screen and on the failed-quiz screen.
requirements.notes: The jokes file content is not in the conversation, so the check is sarcastic-joke presence across multiple points, not the exact wording.

requirements.source_phrase: 1) the puzzle (the user has to put the pieces together to pass to the next level)
requirements.statement: At level 1, tapping one puzzle piece and then a second swaps the two pieces' positions on the board, and the two pieces visibly exchange places.
requirements.notes: Build context: pieces carry data-testid puzzle-piece-{position} and a background-position derived from the piece id, so a swap must move the slice with the piece.

requirements.statement: The puzzle data served with the build gives each piece a distinct slice of the picture (a background-position derived from the piece id) so no two pieces show the same slice and the board holds the complete set of pieces.
requirements.notes: Build context note: reading inline style backgroundPosition is how the solved order can be computed.

requirements.source_phrase: 1) the puzzle (the user has to put the pieces together to pass to the next level)
requirements.statement: When level 1 opens, the pieces are out of their solved positions, so at least one swap is required before the board can be complete.
requirements.notes: A puzzle that opens already solved would make the level meaningless.

requirements.source_phrase: the user has to put the pieces together to pass to the next level
requirements.statement: When every piece sits in its correct position the puzzle shows completion and the game moves on to level 2, and while any piece is out of place the level offers no way to advance.
requirements.notes: Pass condition of level 1.

requirements.source_phrase: 2) the quiz (Q&A after the training from the storyline in the beginning)
requirements.statement: At level 2 each question shows its answer options in a shuffled order, exactly one option is that question's correct answer, and choosing it is recorded as correct while choosing any other option is recorded as wrong.
requirements.notes: Build context: correct answer text equals QUIZ[x].a[0] in data.js; options are shuffled, so correctness must compare text, not position.

requirements.statement: The quiz data served with the build defines each question's text, its answer list with the correct answer at index 0, and a pass mark, so the screen can mark an answer correct by comparing the chosen option text against that entry.
requirements.notes: Mechanism the quiz screen depends on.

requirements.source_phrase: Q&A after the training from the storyline in the beginning
requirements.statement: Every quiz question asks about a fact the training/storyline shown earlier states, so a player who read the intro can answer it from that content alone, and no question depends on a fact never shown.
requirements.notes: The user ties the quiz to the training; a question grounded in nothing shown breaks that promise.

requirements.source_phrase: **Reia quiz-ul cu o glumă de la B.O.B.**
requirements.statement: Failing the quiz (answering below the pass mark) shows a screen with a B.O.B. joke and a retry control, and pressing retry restarts the quiz at question one with the score reset to zero and the option orders reshuffled.
requirements.notes: Build context: quiz-retry-btn.

requirements.source_phrase: 3) the problems & solutions (after the rocket decollated, different malfunctions appear and the user has to select different types of components needed to be repaired)
requirements.statement: At level 3, after launch, each malfunction is shown with its component options and the player selects one to repair it; selecting the correct component marks that malfunction repaired and the level moves on to the next malfunction.
requirements.notes: Build context: repair options carry testid repair-option-{key}; MALFUNCTIONS data holds the correct key.

requirements.statement: The malfunction data served with the build lists each malfunction with its description, its option list and exactly one correct repair key, and the full set of malfunctions a run must repair is the set the data defines (the build describes eight).
requirements.notes: The brief does not state eight; the build description does, so the count is recorded as build-derived and must match the served data.

requirements.statement: The third wrong repair choice at level 3 ends the level with the rocket-explosion sequence and the lose path, while a first or second wrong choice gives feedback and lets the player keep repairing.
requirements.notes: Exact loss rule the user gave when asked.

requirements.source_phrase: 1: cel fericit, în care user-ul câștigă și nivelul 3, apoi apărem noi - pozele din arhivă - cu mesajul de „Congratulations! Welcome to the colony Gratziella”
requirements.statement: Repairing every malfunction correctly ends level 3 in the happy ending, which displays the text 'Congratulations! Welcome to the colony Gratziella' together with the colony characters' photographs.
requirements.notes: Wording of the message is fixed by the user.

requirements.source_phrase: racheta explodează, robotul B.O.B. - care era mereu sarcastic - plutește prin spațiu, ajunge pe Marte și pune o floare la mormânt, și un final semi-amuzant - „Stoooopids!”
requirements.statement: Failing level 3 plays the sad ending in order: the rocket explodes, B.O.B. floats through space, reaches Mars, places a flower on a grave, and the ending text 'Stoooopids!' appears.
requirements.notes: Build description: about 16 seconds of auto-advancing phases and a lose-continue control.

requirements.source_phrase: noi, cele 6 persoane din colonie (Queen Gratziella și cei 5 locatari ai coloniei) apărem la final, indiferent dacă este trist sau nu
requirements.statement: Both the win ending and the lose ending show exactly six colony characters, Queen Gratziella plus the five colonists, each with its own photograph and name.
requirements.notes: The user insists the colony appears regardless of outcome.

requirements.statement: The six colony photographs are six distinct files served by the app, each mapped to one named character (Queen Gratziella and the five colonists), returning HTTP 200 with a non-zero image body.
requirements.notes: Attachment archive of colony character art; two characters sharing one photo would break the promise of six people.

requirements.source_phrase: la final de tot, indiferent dacă se câștigă sau se pierde, să apară credits (numele creatorilor: Andreea Vladu, Maria Cojocaru, Ionuț Ivanici, Goran Giuchici, Patrick Drăghina)
requirements.statement: After either ending, and whether the run was won or lost, a credits screen appears and lists exactly Andreea Vladu, Maria Cojocaru, Ionuț Ivanici, Goran Giuchici, Patrick Drăghina, with no name missing and no extra name.
requirements.notes: Build description: credits have a skip control; the final wait-free path must still show them.

requirements.statement: The credits content served with the build lists exactly those five names in the order given, and the stage machine reaches the credits stage from both the win and the lose branches.
requirements.notes: Checks the names and both endings at the data/stage level.

requirements.statement: Simple sound effects play on the game's key actions (a piece swap, a correct repair, a wrong repair, the explosion), each triggered effect is a real audio file of non-zero duration, and no trigger throws an error in the console.
requirements.notes: User chose simple sound effects when asked.

requirements.source_phrase: **Să fie un joc distractiv pentru copii de gimnaziu, cu o personaje și o temă de tipul cartoon.**
requirements.statement: Every screen uses the supplied cartoon character art and a cartoon-styled theme (illustrated characters, playful display type), with no stock photography and no screen left showing an empty placeholder box instead of art.
requirements.notes: The 'fun' part of the sentence is subjective; the cartoon theme and character art are the testable half.

requirements.statement: Level 1 cannot be bypassed: with pieces out of place there is no control that advances the game, and a swap that moves a correctly placed piece out of place returns the board to incomplete so the level does not complete.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'a record can be created' for the level-completion action.

requirements.statement: Answering a quiz question wrongly marks that option wrong on screen, does not count toward the pass mark, and the quiz moves on to the next question without ending the run.
requirements.notes: Inverse of the correctness rule; a wrong answer must not be scored as correct.

requirements.statement: A wrong repair at level 3 tells the player in B.O.B.'s terms that the choice was wrong, leaves that malfunction unrepaired and the rest of the list unchanged, and moves the visible mistake count from 0 to 1 and then to 2 before the third attempt ends the level.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of the three-mistakes rule: the counter must be visible and must not skip or double-count.

requirements.statement: The explosion/lose sequence advances through its phases on its own within a bounded time and offers a continue control that reaches the colony scene and then the credits, so a losing player is never left on a stuck or blank screen.
requirements.notes: Build description: about 16 s of auto phases plus lose-continue-btn; sports a real risk of a dead end.

requirements.statement: Level 3 ends only by repairing every malfunction correctly (win) or by the third wrong repair (lose); no other control, page refresh or navigation moves the game from level 3 into an ending.
requirements.notes: State-machine rule for the level the user called most important.

requirements.statement: After the credits a play-again control restarts the game at the title screen with the mistake count, cargo manifest, quiz score, puzzle board and score all reset, so the new run begins from zero.
requirements.notes: Build description lists 'play again'; stale state across runs would corrupt every later level.

requirements.statement: At the cargo stage the player loads items into the rocket and the manifest shows a running total mass in kg; launch is blocked with a message naming the problem (over 100 kg, or a required category missing) until oxygen, water, food and parts are all loaded and the total is at most 100 kg.
requirements.notes: Build description: cargo must carry oxygen, water, food and parts under 100 kg, rocks preloaded so they must be removed. Not in the user's words; derived from the build and the mission-design archetype.

requirements.statement: The cargo logic shipped with the build defines each item's mass in kg and a single 100 kg limit; the total is the exact sum of the loaded items' masses, and the launch stage is reachable only when the manifest passes the same rule the screen displays.
requirements.notes: Mechanism the cargo screen and the launch gate depend on.

requirements.statement: The cargo manifest starts with rocks already loaded; removing a rock lowers the running total by that rock's mass and adding a required item raises it by that item's mass, with the displayed total matching the visible item list after every change.
requirements.notes: Build description: rocks preloaded so the player must remove them; tests the total as the sum of its parts.

requirements.statement: The score shown at the end of a run equals the sum of the points the game awards for that run (quiz correct answers and correct repairs), is the same whole number on the ending screen, the leaderboard entry and after a reload, and a run with zero correct answers shows 0 rather than blank.
requirements.notes: The scoring formula is not stated in the brief; the requirement fixes the identity (one total, shown everywhere, equal to its parts) and leaves the weights open - assumption recorded so Phase 4 can flag a total that disagrees across screens.

requirements.statement: At 1920x800 and at 390x844 every screen (title, dialogue, puzzle, quiz, cargo, launch, level 3, both endings, colony, credits, leaderboard) shows its primary content and controls visible without overlap, clipping or horizontal scrolling.
requirements.notes: Two viewports named in the testing brief; cartoon art makes overlap likely on the phone width.

requirements.statement: Body text on every screen meets a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background in the shipped theme, including dialogue text over illustrated scenes and the credits text.
requirements.notes: Dark space backgrounds with coloured cartoon text are a known contrast risk.

requirements.statement: A character or colony image that fails to load shows a labelled fallback inside its frame instead of a broken-image icon or an empty hole, and the surrounding layout does not collapse.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'a value is displayed': a missing art file must not blank the scene.

requirements.statement: Every user action answers on screen in the player's terms: a correct or wrong repair is labelled, a blocked launch says why, a score submission confirms or explains the failure, and each long sequence (launch, explosion) shows progress and ends - nothing succeeds or fails silently.
requirements.notes: Tier 2 UX class; the build has several timed multi-phase sequences.

requirements.statement: Product copy matches the brief: the robot is written 'B.O.B.', the colony 'Gratziella', the endings use exactly 'Congratulations! Welcome to the colony Gratziella' and 'Stoooopids!', and the title screen names the NASA Space Apps challenge mission.
requirements.notes: Fixed strings the user wrote verbatim; the NASA page reference is only carried as the mission framing.

requirements.statement: Reloading the browser at any stage, or opening any URL path of the app, returns a rendered screen with working controls (title screen or the resumed stage), never a blank page, a 404 or a crash.
requirements.notes: Single-page stage machine with no router; a deep link or refresh is the common failure.

requirements.statement: A selected puzzle piece, a selected repair option and an item added to the cargo manifest each look visibly different from their unselected state, and the launch control looks disabled until the manifest is valid and looks enabled once it is.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'a control exists': operating it must change the control itself.

requirements.statement: Each skip control (dialogue skip, credits skip) moves the game forward exactly once per press, does not skip past the stage it belongs to, and leaves the stage machine in the state that control promises.
requirements.notes: Build description: data-testid dialogue-skip-btn and a credits skip; a skip that lands nowhere is a common bug.

requirements.statement: At the end of a run the player can enter a name and submit the score; the screen confirms the submission and the name and score appear on the leaderboard with the value just played.
requirements.notes: Build description: leaderboard shows score, backend POST/GET /api/scores. Not in the user's words.

requirements.statement: POST /api/scores stores the submitted name and score and refuses a payload with no name or a negative or non-numeric score without storing anything; GET /api/scores returns the stored scores highest first, each exactly once, and both survive a backend restart.
requirements.notes: Only server surface in the build (backend/server.py).

requirements.statement: A score submitted at the end of a run is still on the leaderboard after a page reload and in a fresh browser session, showing the same name and the same number.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of persistence; a leaderboard held only in browser state would fail.

requirements.statement: A leaderboard with no stored scores shows an explicit empty message rather than a blank panel or a spinner, and with many scores it lists every stored score once, highest first, scrolled or paged.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'a list is shown': zero rows and a thousand rows.

requirements.statement: GET /api/scores orders results by score descending with a stable tie order, and its list holds exactly the rows the store contains - no duplicate, no dropped row, and no row whose value differs from what was posted.
requirements.notes: A value shown must equal the stored value it is labelled as.

requirements.statement: Each triggered sound effect plays through the browser's audio for a non-zero duration and stops on its own; when the game is muted no sound plays and no playback error is thrown.
requirements.notes: Sound is only meaningful if the served files actually decode and play.

requirements.statement: Leaving and re-entering the dialogue, launch and explosion stages starts one timer per stage, so a run replayed several times advances each phase once and never double-counts a repair mistake or double-advances a dialogue line.
requirements.notes: Resource-leak class for a stage machine driven by timers.

requirements.statement: The stage machine clears the interval or timeout of the stage it leaves, so a session that enters and leaves a timed stage ten times holds exactly one pending timer for the current stage.
requirements.notes: Logic-level form of the timer leak requirement.

requirements.statement: The frontend calls the scores API at the base URL taken from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL at build time, no hardcoded host or port appears in the served bundle, and a request to that base returns the scores JSON with CORS allowed for the app's origin.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class; the frontend URL comes from /app/frontend/.env REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.

requirements.statement: Every level screen shows which of the three levels the player is in and how far through it they are (pieces placed, questions answered, malfunctions repaired), and that indicator moves as the player acts.
requirements.notes: benchmark: story-driven level games always show level number and progress within the level

requirements.statement: Each quiz answer is marked right or wrong immediately, the correct option is revealed on a wrong answer, and a running correct-answer count is visible for the length of the quiz.
requirements.notes: benchmark: quiz games mark each answer and show a running score

requirements.statement: The puzzle screen shows the completed picture as a small reference image so the player can see the target arrangement.
requirements.notes: benchmark: jigsaw-style puzzles show the finished image as reference

requirements.statement: A visible sound on/off control is present on every screen or in a persistent corner, changes its own state when pressed, and the muted state survives a level change and a page reload.
requirements.notes: benchmark: children's games always offer a mute toggle, and its state persists

requirements.statement: A restart control reachable during play returns the player to the title screen after a confirmation, and the next start begins a fresh run.
requirements.notes: benchmark: games offer restart/quit from inside a level

requirements.statement: The score submission accepts a player name of 1 to 20 characters, refuses an empty name with a message, and shows the name on the leaderboard exactly as typed.
requirements.notes: benchmark: arcade-style leaderboards take a name and echo it back unchanged

requirements.statement: When the scores API is unreachable or returns an error, the ending screen still completes, tells the player in plain language that the score could not be saved, and play again still works.
requirements.notes: Product-shell failure path: the only network call in the game must not dead-end the run.

requirements.statement: Passing the quiz plays a short post-quiz dialogue scene before the cargo stage, and the player can advance or skip it into the next stage.
requirements.notes: Build description: 'post quiz dialog' stage between the quiz and cargo.

requirements.statement: Pressing launch starts a launch animation of a few seconds with visible progress, the launch control shows a busy or disabled state while it runs and cannot be pressed twice, and the game then enters level 3.
requirements.notes: Build description: launch-btn runs about 7 s before level 3; double-press is the obvious failure.

unmapped_phrases.phrase: Să fie un joc distractiv pentru copii de gimnaziu
unmapped_phrases.reason: 'fun' has no objective specification; the cartoon-theme, sound and dialogue requirements carry the testable part of the sentence.

unmapped_phrases.phrase: Take into consideration the information from the project page: https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/space-mission-design-game/
unmapped_phrases.reason: the linked page is not in the conversation, so its content cannot be turned into assertions; only the NASA mission framing is carried, by the copy requirement.

unmapped_phrases.phrase: using the details Nasa project page and the attached files (the characters, the puzzle, the quiz)
unmapped_phrases.reason: the zip attachments (character art, initial materials, Bob jokes) are not available here, so their exact lines, images and puzzle picture cannot be asserted; the structural and language requirements cover what is testable.
an emphasis and tone request with no observable behaviour.
